paragraph: On 14 August 2026 [twelve counters were working in the 11 municipalities of Zaire province](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/zaire-instala-antenas-v-sat-nas-comunas-para-funcionamento-dos-buap/>), the provincial director said. The Ministry of Territorial Administration [runs a national programme of V/SAT satellite antennas for commune seats](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/zaire-instala-antenas-v-sat-nas-comunas-para-funcionamento-dos-buap/>). In the last twelve months [the data update began on 15 June 2026 with 254 counters in a first phase and 634 intended](<https://novojornal.co.ao/politica/detalhe/eleicoes-2027-arranca-hoje-a-prova-de-vida-para-actualizacao-do-registo-eleitoral-72520.html>). No national count of municipalities with a working counter has been found. Nothing found says how the counters at municipal seats are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

In October 2026 Butihinda commune's accountants and tax collectors were [entering its revenue and spending into AK-SOFT](<https://communebutihinda.gov.bi/butihinda-la-digitalisation-de-la-gestion-comptable-budgetaire-et-financiere-se-modernise-grace-au-logiciel-ak-soft/>), a financial-management platform. They said they need a stable Internet connection. In the last twelve months, in the same month, [the Primature trained communal finance officers on AK-SOFT](<https://communebutihinda.gov.bi/butihinda-la-digitalisation-de-la-gestion-comptable-budgetaire-et-financiere-se-modernise-grace-au-logiciel-ak-soft/>). The sector strategy of February 2021 [names the extension of the government's fibre-optic interconnection to the communes under its e-government project](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Burundi/Sektoralnaa%20strategia%20v%20oblasti%20IKT%20do%202027%20g.%20prinata%20v%202021.pdf>). No source found says how Butihinda's office is connected or how many communes are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of communes connected by the state.

In 2024 town halls [used the services of the Réseau National de l'Administration](<https://odd.finances.bj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Benin_Rapport-dallocation-et-dimpact-Eurobond-ODD_2025.pdf>), the state's own network. The finance ministry counts [12 new town halls using the network's services in 2024](<https://odd.finances.bj/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Benin_Rapport-dallocation-et-dimpact-Eurobond-ODD_2025.pdf>), and Benin has 77 communes. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the state agency ASIN [presented the connection of Bantè's mairie to the network at its town hall](<https://lemondelocal.bj/bante-le-maire-daniel-fatchehoun-et-lasin-posent-les-jalons-dune-administration-communale-moderne-et-connectee/>). On 11 September 2026 [a connection failure hit several of Cotonou's arrondissement offices](<https://lepatriotebenin.com/index.php/2026/09/16/paiement-des-droit-taxi-quand-la-connexion-cree-denormes-prejudices-aux-usagers/>). No cumulative total of town halls on the network has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of town halls connected by the state.

In January 2024 ANPTIC listed [the interconnection of local governments' buildings to RESINA](<https://anptic.gov.bf/nos-realisations/>), the government network. The territorial administration ministry gives [78 principal civil status centres networked in 2025](<https://www.wakatsera.com/strategie-nationale-de-letat-civil-2023-2027-plus-de-81-dexecution-financiere-enregistres-en-2025/>). In the last twelve months those results were validated on 25 June 2026. ANPTIC's report for 2020 had named [five town halls on RESINA or being put on it](<https://assises-resina.gov.bf/images/Rapport_annuel_2020_ANPTIC_Version_finale_septembre_2021_compressed-2.pdf>). No share of the 351 communes' town halls connected has been found, and the 78 centres are a count with no total. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

BoFiNet's annual report for financial year 2022/23 records [partnerships between BoFiNet and four local authorities](<https://www.bofinet.co.bw/uploads/218/01M004DM8X2QP95FSJHKFK8XAM.pdf>) to deploy premises Wi-Fi in their Rural Administration Centres. The four are [Serowe and Mahalapye District Councils and Bobirwa and Boteti Sub District Councils](<https://www.bofinet.co.bw/uploads/218/01M004DM8X2QP95FSJHKFK8XAM.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The partnerships stood in March 2023. No source states that a council's own office has a connection in use, or gives the total of councils. Establishing would need some council offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

The Central African Republic's universal service fund [was not yet in operation on 15 April 2026](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2104-137723-centrafrique-la-mise-en-uvre-effective-du-fonds-du-service-universel-prevue-pour-2026>), Agence Ecofin reports. Its framework provides for [broadband internet access in mairies](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2104-137723-centrafrique-la-mise-en-uvre-effective-du-fonds-du-service-universel-prevue-pour-2026>). In the last twelve months ARCEP presented a draft budget of 6.2 billion FCFA on 15 April 2026 and said the fund's effective set-up was planned for 2026. The committee that manages the fund [began its activities in July 2025](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2104-137723-centrafrique-la-mise-en-uvre-effective-du-fonds-du-service-universel-prevue-pour-2026>). No source found states that any mairie is connected, or gives a count or share of communes. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

On 17 October 2025 Côte d'Ivoire and IDA [concluded the loan agreement for PADCI phase 1](<https://www.bilan.gouv.ci/actualite/19406>). The project [runs from 2025 to 2030 and carries US$45 million for broadband to targeted public institutions](<https://www.bilan.gouv.ci/actualite/19406>), town halls among them. In the last twelve months, on 4 February 2026, the Council of Ministers [ratified the loan of 84,356,070,200 FCFA by decree](<https://www.bilan.gouv.ci/actualite/19406>). No source found states a town hall connected and in use, or gives a count or share of town halls connected. Establishing would need some town hall offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

In August 2026 UNDP Cameroon [stated an internet connection at two East Region commune offices](<https://www.undp.org/cameroon/stories/dans-lest-du-cameroun-la-digitalisation-de-letat-civil-transforme-progressivement-lacces-lidentite-legale-bertoua-cameroun-aout-2026>): Bétaré-Oya, where it is unstable, and Bertoua 1er. In the last twelve months, on 2 June 2026, the government [presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion programme to connect and equip local authorities](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/cameroon-launches-163-million-push-to-digitize-local-governments>), and its financing was still being sought. Cameroon has [360 communes and 14 urban communities](<https://journalcentrifuge.com/societe/534-digitalisation-des-communes-et-villes-camerounaises-la-premiere-phase-du-programme-presentee-a-yaounde>). No share or total of communes connected has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

On 17 March 2026 the governor of Haut-Uélé [handed satellite kits to the heads of the province's decentralised entities](<https://acp.cd/economie/haut-uele-des-kits-internet-satellite-starlink-aux-institutions-pour-renforcer-la-communication>) at Isiro. They went to [45 chiefdoms and sectors of Haut-Uélé](<https://acp.cd/economie/haut-uele-des-kits-internet-satellite-starlink-aux-institutions-pour-renforcer-la-communication>), beside 6 territories. In the last twelve months, on 4 June 2026, the national project unit [issued a tender to connect the buildings of 7 governorates and 44 territories](<https://www.mediacongo.net/dpics/filesmanager/jobaof/2026/06-juin/01/ugptn_260604_01_05.pdf>) in a pilot phase. No source found says any chiefdom, sector or commune office works over a connection. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

The World Bank's appraisal of May 2022 [expects shared connectivity to be supplied to decentralised local authorities](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/804131654274496053/pdf/Congo-Republic-of-Congo-Digital-Acceleration-Project.pdf>) under the Patn digital project. In the last twelve months, on 26 February 2026, the project's steering committee [recommended continuing and intensifying the extension of internet access](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-numerique-le-budget-du-patn-pour-lexercice-2026-arrete-a-21872-milliards-de-fcfa/>). [It approved reallocating funds towards the connectivity component](<https://www.aci.cg/congo-numerique-le-budget-du-patn-pour-lexercice-2026-arrete-a-21872-milliards-de-fcfa/>). No source found says any town hall is connected: no count, share or place is given. Establishing would need some town hall offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

On 6 October 2025 NOSi, a public enterprise, said that [21 of the 22 municipalities, all but Mosteiros, were receiving its services regularly](<https://www.balai.cv/noticias/nosi-garante-total-flexibilidade-negocial-junto-das-camaras-municipais-para-evitar-disrupcao-dos-servicos-digitais/>). NOSi's plan of March 2020 [lists the municipal councils' local area networks among those served by basic access to the state's private network](<https://nosi.cv/documents/20121/1141867/nosi-pa-global-estrategico-2019-2022.pdf/c3749473-6a40-8f4f-7b9d-ca2d353b0e8a>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of councils connected has been found. The source of the 21 of 22 does not say how their offices are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

In February 2024 the civil-status centres of Djibouti city's three communes [recorded civil-status events in SIGEC](<https://expertise-france.gestmax.fr/_expertise_france/public_files/mdj-tdr-diagnostic-etat-civil-vf.pdf>), the city's computerised system. They are in Balbala, Ras Dika and Boulaos. The records they enter [sit on a central server at the town hall](<https://expertise-france.gestmax.fr/_expertise_france/public_files/mdj-tdr-diagnostic-etat-civil-vf.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states how the centres are connected, or places a local government office outside Djibouti city on a connection. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

The interior ministry's presentation of June 2019 shows [1,541 commune databases on the civil-status network](<https://www.id4africa.com/2019_event/presentations/InF3/4-Abderrazak-Henni-MOI-Algeria.pdf>), the ministry's own, which is 1,541 of 1,541 communes. In the last twelve months, on 5 April 2026, municipal services [began the third phase of generalising the national vehicle-registration system](<https://www.elmoudjahid.dz/fr/actualite/immatriculation-des-vehicules-passage-au-tout-numerique-des-aujourd-hui-250065>). The phase ends manual and local procedures. The commune of Bouira [bears its own annual internet subscription](<https://ccomptes.dz/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/RA.2025-AR.pdf>), the Court of Accounts found in September 2023. No count of communes connected after June 2019 has been found, and no current plan with a stated period. Operating would need a current plan or budget line for the communes' connection.

On 15 January 2024 Egypt's minister of communications named a [project to automate local administration and governorate headquarters](<https://www.dostor.org/4607148>). It is to [start at governorate headquarters, move to governorate capitals and districts, and end with local units](<https://www.dostor.org/4607148>). [Minya was chosen as the pilot](<https://www.dostor.org/4607148>), and [the link was expected during 2024](<https://www.dostor.org/4607148>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says whether the Minya link was made, or whether any local unit office is connected. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

In the last twelve months, on 5 December 2025, Addis Ababa's mayor [launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_7858122>). He said implementation would start in 50 of the city's woredas on 8 December. On 22 December 2025 a government statement said [connectivity has been created from the central level down to the woreda level](<https://www.gcs.gov.et/en/2025/12/22/digital-ethiopia-2025-has-brought-about-a-significant-change-in-improving-access-to-civil-registration-and-citizenship-services/>) for civil registration. It called this [a major pilot, in Addis Ababa only](<https://www.gcs.gov.et/en/2025/12/22/digital-ethiopia-2025-has-brought-about-a-significant-change-in-improving-access-to-civil-registration-and-citizenship-services/>). No woreda office outside Addis Ababa has been found on a connection provided to it. Establishing would need some offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

Gabon Review reported on 1 April 2026 that the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem [is on the RAG](<https://www.gabonreview.com/le-rag-operationnel-a-oyem-laninf-accelere-la-modernisation-administrative-en/>), the Réseau de l'Administration Gabonaise, a fibre network. ANINF brought it into service there. In the last twelve months this activation followed fibre that was [installed in 2010 and inactive until ANINF brought it into service](<https://www.gabonreview.com/le-rag-operationnel-a-oyem-laninf-accelere-la-modernisation-administrative-en/>). Gabonclic.info reported in June 2025 that [Akanda and Owendo are linked to the RAG by fibre](<https://gabonclic.info/digitalisation-des-services-municipaux-hermann-immongault-echange-avec-les-delegues-speciaux-dakanda-et-dowendo/>). No total of communes connected or to be connected has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

In February 2024 the communications minister's table [gives the assemblies 274 of 274 planned sites connected](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/FEB-2024-PRESS-BRIEFING_MOCD.pdf>) to the government network, within [950 of 951 government sites](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/FEB-2024-PRESS-BRIEFING_MOCD.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 3 September 2026, the Local Government Service [signed a memorandum of understanding with Celltel Networks](<https://adomonline.com/local-government-service-partners-celltel-networks-to-drive-digital-transformation/>). Its head [described the state the Service is moving from as "disconnected offices"](<https://adomonline.com/local-government-service-partners-celltel-networks-to-drive-digital-transformation/>). Nothing found says how many of the 261 assemblies the 274 sites cover. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

Enabel, the Belgian development agency, [issued the tender of 27 July 2022 for the internet connection of 10 pilot communes](<https://www.piaafrica.com/fr/emplois/guinee/appel-doffre-marche-de-service-pour-la-connexion-internet-de-10-communes-et-des-autres-acteurs-du-projet-pilote-de-digitalisation-de-letat-civil>). Its evaluation draws on fieldwork in April 2026. It says [civil-status officers and data-entry agents at civil registry centres work in the national civil register's central database](<https://open.enabel.be/en/evaluation/39/download/162>), with paper still used in parallel. In the last twelve months, the [relocation of the system's data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted service to commune offices](<https://mosaiqueguinee.com/2026/09/etat-civil-la-guinee-confrontee-a-une-penurie-dactes-de-naissance-numeriques/>), reported on 2 September 2026. No delivery under the tender has been found, and no count of communes connected. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past the pilot, or working in a national system.

[IFMIS, the government's Integrated Financial Management Information System, had been implemented in all Local Government Area Councils by the end of 2024](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/2024-PFM-Annual-Progress-Report.pdf>), on the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs' report. The report names eight councils. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 [describes IFMIS in use or being installed at four of them](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/SECOND-and-THIRD-QUARTER-PFM-PERFORMANCE-REPORT-1-1.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of councils with a connection provided to the office has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

In 2024 the World Bank's digital economy diagnostic stated that [the government's central network does not extend to local government branches](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). It adds that [many ministries at the centre operate on manual systems, and that this is more pronounced at the local level](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). In the last twelve months, on 18 December 2025, Gabon's Council of Ministers approved [an agreement to interconnect the fibre-optic networks of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea](<https://fonction-publique.gouv.ga/object.getObject.do?id=2632&mime=file-mime&object=file>). These are the two countries' national networks. No programme to connect local government offices has been found. Preparing would need a programme prepared or piloted, with equipment handed over, a contract signed or pilot offices connected.

The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy states [the counties were connected by secure connections into the national private governmental voice and data network](<https://ict.go.ke/last-mile-county-connectivity-project-lmccp>). It calls the network NOFBI. The last county was connected by 2017. In the last twelve months, on 25 August 2026, the National Treasury set a deadline of 30 September 2026 for [all 47 county governments to finish integrating the national electronic procurement platform with its financial management system](<https://www.wearetech.africa/actualites/fils/actualites/gestion-publique/kenya-les-47-comtes-sommes-de-passer-aux-marches-publics-numeriques>). No share of county offices connected has been found since 2017. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

No stage is set. As at 30 September 2026, no source found says whether any local government office has a connection of its own, how it is connected, or what it does over the connection. No programme to connect the offices has been found, and no count or share of local governments connected. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Staff working on their own phones or modems would not change this. Absent would need a dated source that states local government offices have no connection of their own.

The Ministry of Local Government's digital transformation project director [said on 2 November 2023 that official e-mail accounts would be created for the heads of administrative units in the municipalities](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=292708&lang=ar>). The ministry runs the system. In October 2025 [the ministry gave the mayors of 21 municipalities access to its electronic systems](<https://alsabaah.ly/%d9%85%d8%ac%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b3-%d8%a8%d9%84%d8%af%d9%8a%d8%a9/>), a count with no total. A 2021 study of three authorities [finds internet access at the authorities' offices that is slow, often disconnected or not always available](<https://eprints.glos.ac.uk/9355/3/9355-Wynn-%282021%29-E-government-and-digital-transformation.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

The e-Government Project built and connected two community council buildings, [under the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology](<https://www.gov.ls/uncategorized/chief-thesele-hands-over-community-councils-buildings/>), and handed them to the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftainship Affairs on 31 July 2019. The Minister said that the two buildings [have the Internet installed](<https://www.gov.ls/uncategorized/chief-thesele-hands-over-community-councils-buildings/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. On 17 June 2024 the ministry's Principal Secretary said its roll-out of 74 digital services [would also connect Community Councils](<https://www.lena.gov.ls/micsti-partners-strategise/>). No number, date or funding was given. Establishing would need councils connected past the pilot, or working in a national system.

An Interior Ministry circular of 19 May 2020 gives a figure for GIR-CT, the revenue system for local authorities. It [was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers](<https://aueks.ma/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Cir-du-Ministre-de-linterieur-N%C2%B0-32-du-19-5-2020-la-mise-en-oeuvre-et-suivi-de-dematerialisation-des-procedures-vers-Zero-papier.pdf>), 60.9 per cent. In the last twelve months, the World Bank's status report of 30 January 2026 counts [59 of 97 participating municipalities with the civil registry back-office system operational](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099030926112020747/pdf/P168147-76ebb47f-2ef4-42ba-8d67-88b617eb1f27.pdf>). A diagnostic of 2016 said municipal councils [equip those offices from their own budgets](<https://id4d.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/2018-04/Morocco_ID4D_Diagnostic_Web404018.pdf>). No source found says the state provides a connection to the commune offices. Operating would need a published share above half.

The [Plan National de Décentralisation Emergente 2023-2030 was validated by decree on 2 August 2023](<https://bdd.pseau.org/outils/ouvrages/mdat_plan_national_de_decentralisation_emergente_2024.pdf>). It appeared in June 2024. It gives a [baseline of 10 per cent of the country's 1,695 communes with direct access to the SIFC over a secure connection](<https://bdd.pseau.org/outils/ouvrages/mdat_plan_national_de_decentralisation_emergente_2024.pdf>). The target is 50 per cent for 2030. On 30 April 2025 the ministry [handed internet boxes and a subscription to all 38 communes of the Antananarivo agglomeration](<https://www.produir-madagascar.mg/remise-des-materiels-informatiques-et-techniques-dans-le-cadre-de-matac-hanorina-phase-2/>). In the last twelve months, communes using the civil registration system SIECM [rose from 75 to 336 in the six months to December 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099121925094025414/txt/P169413-92234883-0626-410f-a2c4-c2b2e93265f7.txt>). Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

The Council of Ministers of 1 June 2022 [adopted a draft decree approving the contract for the Projet d'Accès au service de télécommunication des collectivités territoriales](<http://news.abamako.com/h/270935.html>). [The contract was awarded to SIMO TELECOM for CFA 9,407,295,000 over twelve months](<http://news.abamako.com/h/270935.html>). The only earlier fact found is a draft strategy of November 2014, which counts the [connection of certain communes as a result achieved under the government's 2005 national ICT policy](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Mali/Nacionalnaa%20strategia%20razvitia%20cifrovoj%20ekonomiki%202020%20prinata%20v%202015.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says any local government office is connected. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past any pilot, or working in a national system.

The European Union's action document of June 2026 says GovNet [has connected about 1,000 public institutions and organs at central level and across 141 districts](<https://www.gtai.de/resource/blob/2006980/32b32750cfcf0c9bab9747e7b5c49ebc/PRO202606172006968%20-%20Annex%202.PDF>). It also says [underinvestment in middle- and last-mile infrastructure leaves many local administrations insufficiently connected](<https://www.gtai.de/resource/blob/2006980/32b32750cfcf0c9bab9747e7b5c49ebc/PRO202606172006968%20-%20Annex%202.PDF>). In the last twelve months, the EU's annual action plan for 2026, dated 17 June 2026, [carries a EUR 7.1 million Team Europe action to expand GovNet in selected districts](<https://www.gtai.de/resource/blob/2006980/32b32750cfcf0c9bab9747e7b5c49ebc/PRO202606172006968%20-%20Annex%202.PDF>). No source found puts a local government office on GovNet. No count of local governments connected has been found. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past any pilot, or working in a national system.

The PEFA assessment of public financial management, dated January 2025, states that SIGeL, the integrated local finance management system, [was deployed in 90 per cent of local authorities at the end of 2023](<https://finances.gov.mr/sites/default/files/2025-01/PEFA%20MAURITANIE%20RAPPORT%20FINAL%20Version%20d%C3%A9finitive-janvier%202025.pdf>). The share is of 232 authorities: 13 regions and 219 communes. Until 2022 the local authorities [ran their budgets in the off-line system El Khazin](<https://finances.gov.mr/sites/default/files/2025-01/PEFA%20MAURITANIE%20RAPPORT%20FINAL%20Version%20d%C3%A9finitive-janvier%202025.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The assessment states no connection for the offices, and no owner, plan or finance for one has been found. Operating would need a published share above half of local governments with a connection provided to the office.

The Ministry of Local Government's report for 2023-2024 says its I-Council project [was piloted at Moka from 27 August 2018](<https://localgovernment.govmu.org/Lists/DocumentsLinks/Attachments/24/Annual%20Report%202023-2024.pdf>). [It took three years to implement in all local authorities](<https://localgovernment.govmu.org/Lists/DocumentsLinks/Attachments/24/Annual%20Report%202023-2024.pdf>). The report says [all employees of the twelve local authority digital offices do their daily tasks in real time](<https://localgovernment.govmu.org/Lists/DocumentsLinks/Attachments/24/Annual%20Report%202023-2024.pdf>). The ministry's [permit table for the year to 30 June 2025 lists all 12](<https://mof.govmu.org/Documents/2026/Annual%20Report%20on%20Performance%20for%20Ministries%20and%20Department/5-1%20Local%20Government/Annual%20Report%202024-2025.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says who provides the offices' connection. Operating would need a connection provided to the office by the state or the authority, shown by a share or a count with its total.

Minutes of consultations with councils in June and July 2024 say [the Department of E-Government manages the councils' internet on the government network](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099091824155589106/pdf/P505095-9d6abe69-a9cf-48cb-bdd8-9140a232f79e.pdf>). The minutes [name Kasungu as on the network](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099091824155589106/pdf/P505095-9d6abe69-a9cf-48cb-bdd8-9140a232f79e.pdf>). They record on 25 June 2024 that Dowa was yet to be connected. In the last twelve months, GIZ Malawi says the government [launched a six-month pilot in mid-June 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/giz-malawi_socialprotection-socialregistry-digitaltransformation-activity-7475071354057256960-qS1N>). In it, District Council Offices in Balaka and Dowa take on-demand updates to the national social registry. No share of the 35 councils connected has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

No stage is set. As at 30 September 2026, no source found says whether any local government office has a connection of its own, how it is connected, or what it does over the connection. No programme to connect the offices has been found, and no count or share of local governments connected. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Staff working on their own phones or modems would not change this. Absent would need a dated source that states local government offices have no connection of their own.

The Projet Villages Intelligents is [financed by the State of Niger and the World Bank at USD 100 million](<https://anp.ne/niger-grace-aux-infrastructures-adaptees-fournies-par-le-pvi-plus-de-900-localites-accedent-a-une-connectivite-numerique-haut-debit/>) and closes on 23 October 2026. On 15 April 2026 the news agency ANP reported the project saying [broadband internet had been extended to 266 communes, 339 health centres and 298 schools](<https://anp.ne/niger-grace-aux-infrastructures-adaptees-fournies-par-le-pvi-plus-de-900-localites-accedent-a-une-connectivite-numerique-haut-debit/>). In the last twelve months, the project's connectivity for the town halls [was officially received at a ceremony on 6 May 2026](<https://www.lesahel.org/ceremonie-officielle-de-reception-de-la-connectivite-des-mairies-une-etape-structurante-dans-la-transformation-numerique-des-collectivites-territoriales-au-niger/>). No share of communes connected has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

The World Bank's BRIDGE project was approved on 6 October 2025. It [sets a target of 3,428 local government administration offices on broadband by September 2030](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099072426133520910/txt/P508383-134fae3d-1255-4dae-b619-aacd0944fa2f.txt>). The Bank [counts 510 local government administration offices connected to broadband at 17 December 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099072426133520910/txt/P508383-134fae3d-1255-4dae-b619-aacd0944fa2f.txt>), the same number as in July 2025. In the last twelve months, the credit was [signed on 30 December 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099012026134023499/txt/P508383-6acad398-4988-4bcd-ba9e-6952f14355ec.txt>). On 22 September 2026 the communications minister [cut the delivery timeline from five years to three](<https://techsoma.africa/nigeria-project-bridge-fibre-network-2028/>). Operating would need more than half of local governments connected, as a published share or a count given with its total.

The Governance and Decentralisation Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029, of 14 November 2024, [costs an intervention giving local government entities ICT equipment and internet connectivity](<https://www.minaloc.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Minaloc/Publications/Policies/Governance___Decentralisation/Governance___Decentralisation_SSP.pdf>). The civil registration system NCI-CRVS was [fully operational at district, sector and cell offices for 2025](<https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2026-04/Rwanda%20Civil%20Registration%20Vital%20Statistics%202025_0.pdf>). It was also [in 2024](<https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2025-04/Rwanda%20Vital%20Statistics%20Report%202024_N.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the Ministry of Local Government stated that births and deaths [are registered at the cell, where before they were at the sector](<https://www.minaloc.gov.rw/news-detail/rwanda-launches-new-integrated-civil-registration-system>). No share or count of district offices connected has been found. No source says who pays for a district office's connection. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

The one statement found is a meeting's recommendation of 22 November 2022, which asked that Sudatel connect by fibre the localities that ask, at their own cost. No locality is reported connected, and nothing has been found on the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local government offices have no connection of their own.

In August 2025 the civil-status agency ANEC said the state company SENUM SA had [put network equipment in on site at 383 centres](<https://www.child-identity.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/PRESENTATIONETATSENEGAL-Aliou-Sall.pdf>). Of these, 235 were in service and connected. In the last twelve months NEKKAL's final steering committee [reported 400 civil registration centres interconnected](<https://aps.sn/le-programme-nekkal-a-permis-dimportantes-avancees-dans-la-modernisation-de-letat-civil/>) on 29 June 2026. On 27 April 2026 ANEC's director general said that in some centres the circuit was never completed. Elsewhere, he said, it is very slow. No share of communes connected has been found. No source sets the 400 centres against a count of communes. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

Its roll-out included the [provision of an internet facility for 21 local councils and a local area network at 21](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Public-Financial-Management-Report-2025.pdf>). In the last twelve months [solar panels and batteries were installed at 18](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Public-Financial-Management-Report-2025.pdf>), and the internet contract is [shown as completed on 18 November 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099063026135010027/pdf/P172492-9bfaf78e-7d6d-4986-8104-9956e09b9d12.pdf>). The report gives no rural share, and no source says who pays for the service afterwards. Mature would need a published share of at least 90 per cent connected and working in national systems, with the rural share.

The National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 set a goal. [All local authorities of the federal government and the member states were to have internet access by its third year](<https://moct.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/National-ICT-Policy-Strategy-2019-2024.pdf>). The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic of 2022 says the finance systems are implemented in [all municipalities](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099045403212411797/txt/IDU105f167fa1085214f8b1919f141249b1e8fae.txt>) of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and the policy's period has ended. No source says how any municipal office is connected. No count of municipalities is given. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

In late 2021 the International Organization for Migration assessed eleven local governments, ten counties and Wau Municipality. [One has a satellite terminal at the Commissioner's office, and ten have none](<https://southsudan.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl1046/files/documents/20220412-ecrp-county-capacity-report_5.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing has been found on any event since 2021. No count of connected offices across all the country's counties has been found. No use is named for the Maban terminal, and nothing says who pays for it. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

The Municipal Council of Mbabane [pays for internet among its utility services](<https://www.mbabane.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/MCM-Annual-Report-22-23.pdf>), in its report for the year to March 2023. In the last twelve months the House of Assembly [gave a second reading on 21 September 2026 to the three Bills enabling the project's loans](<https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P508948>). COMESA reports that from January to June 2026 [the project was in preparation, with its infrastructure assessment begun](<https://idea.comesa.int/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IDEA-Biannual-implementation-Progress-January-to-June-2026-V-J20-FK-006.pdf>). No share of local governments with a connected office is published. No Tinkhundla centre is reported connected. It gives 265 ministries, departments, agencies and local authorities on it as one figure.
